title: Firebase fixtures (generated)
description: Recorded output of the benchmark's fixture generators whose credential family belongs to the provider Firebase. Each fixture projects a Case or a fixture-plan cell and carries its own evidence entry; the set is organised by provider, not by how the legacy benchmark grouped its suites.

ev-81a6be7de4.rationale: The 152-character token in each of these fixtures is inside the token grammar: literal AAAA, 7 head characters, a ':' separator, then exactly 140 body characters, all head and body characters from [A-Za-z0-9_-] in every respect. Consistency only, not a provider rule. Three open-source rule artifacts from three different maintainers, each pinned to a commit and located by line, define the same token grammar. No provider-owned page that was read states this format; a January 2017 Firebase blog post gives a 175-character total and an example key header beginning AU for keys of that time, which is not reconciled here and stays an open question. Scanner output on these fixtures and agreement among scanners are not used. This is an evidence-class statement, not a support-status decision. Synthetic values; no liveness or issuance claim. The artifacts speak to the token's own shape and not to the surrounding syntax (environment file, curl, YAML, code, log line).

ev-88902c26fd.rationale: The provider's web client page says the console shows the public key string of the web push key pair, and its code sample marks the value passed as vapidKey as 'the public key generated from the Firebase console' (register(); for the deprecated token APIs the same key is passed to getToken()). The fixture puts a value in the vapidKey option of a getToken call. That the value in that position is the public half of the key pair is the provider's statement; that a public key is not a secret credential follows by a step a reviewer can repeat (it is the half the page tells developers to put in client code). The page states no length or encoding for the key and says nothing about server keys; no claim is made that the fixture value is a real key. Evidence-class statement only, not a support-status decision.

sources.supports: States that the console displays the public key string of the generated key pair and that the vapidKey option is filled with the public key generated from the console (register(), and getToken() for the deprecated token APIs).
